title: The Death of the Chatbot: Why Your Dataverse Strategy Is Broken
description:
Many organizations celebrate early Copilot and chatbot wins, then discover agents borrowing human identities, calling models directly and running long after their projects ended. This episode is for architects, IT and governance leaders who want to scale AI agents safely, explaining how identity, ontologies, a governance hub with a model gateway, observability and Agent 365 form the landing zone that turns scattered chatbots into a managed platform.
In this episode
00:00 – Intro: chat isn't a platform01:57 – The Copilot illusion and governance debt06:04 – Identity and reasoning: agent IDs, RAG and ontologies20:37 – What an AI landing zone actually is25:13 – The model gateway and the ontology layer40:26 – Agent 365 as the control plane and the governance hub50:41 – Data residency, FinOps, multi-cloud and ghost agents85:07 – Security, transition strategy and autonomous operations
Key takeaways
Copilot and chatbots are features, not a platform: scaling AI agents without identity, policy enforcement and logging creates governance debt that compounds with every new team.An AI landing zone combines a traceable identity plane (agent IDs), a governance hub with a model gateway, and a shared ontology-based data plane so agents reason consistently over business relationships instead of text fragments.Agent 365 as a control plane adds registry, policy enforcement, observability and lifecycle management across clouds, enabling cost control, preventive compliance and retirement of ghost agents.
